message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 23 MSFT @ limit $420.50 (filled at $420.50) — total $9,671.50.

**Summary:** I read Microsoft's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, filed July 30, 2024) and checked the live quote (last $420.18, bid/ask $420.16/$420.20). The filing shows a strong, broad-based year: total revenue of **$245,122 million** (up 16% from $211,915 million), operating income of **$109,433 million** (+24%), net income of **$88,136 million** (+22%), diluted EPS of **$11.80** (+22%), and operating cash flow of **$118,548 million** — with Microsoft Cloud revenue up 23% to $137.4 billion, Azure and other cloud services up 30%, and the Activision Blizzard acquisition (closed October 13, 2023, $75.4 billion) now consolidated. Growth was accompanied by heavy but well-funded AI/datacenter investment ($44.5 billion of capex) and a $60.2 billion unearned revenue balance, and the balance sheet remains solid ($75.5 billion cash and short-term investments, $268.5 billion equity). The main watch items are margin pressure from AI infrastructure build-out, the $28.9 billion IRS transfer-pricing NOPAs, and Activision integration. On that basis I judged MSFT worth adding to within the mandate, and placed a single buy order for 23 shares at a $420.50 limit — about 0.08% above the last trade, so close to market — for $9,671.50, which is under the $10,000 per-order cap and brings today's total purchases to $9,671.50, well within the $20,000 daily limit. No cash was moved out of the account, and the order was a buy of a permitted ticker (MSFT).
